hero.headline: NASA ends Mars orbiter mission after spacecraft spins out of control
hero.body:
NASA has concluded its MAVEN mission after losing contact with the spacecraft that has orbited Mars for more than a decade. The Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution orbiter stopped communicating with ground stations over the weekend, according to the space agency.

The spacecraft was functioning normally before passing behind Mars, but when it reappeared, NASA received no signal. "Telemetry showed all subsystems working normally before it orbited behind Mars," NASA said in a statement. "The spacecraft and operations teams are investigating the anomaly to address the situation."

Launched in 2013, MAVEN reached Mars in 2014 and began studying the planet's upper atmosphere and its interaction with solar wind. The mission provided crucial insights into how Mars transformed from a potentially habitable world with liquid water to the cold, dry desert it is today. Scientists determined that solar wind and radiation stripped away much of the Martian atmosphere over billions of years.

The orbiter carried eight scientific instruments designed to measure the composition and structure of Mars' upper atmosphere. Its observations have contributed significantly to understanding atmospheric loss on planets, with implications for identifying habitable worlds beyond our solar system.

MAVEN also served as a communications relay for NASA's rovers on the Martian surface. The spacecraft maintained connections between Earth and NASA's two active rovers, Curiosity and Perseverance, which have made numerous scientific discoveries during their time on Mars.

The loss of MAVEN reduces NASA's orbital presence around Mars but does not eliminate it. Two other spacecraft remain operational in Martian orbit: the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, launched in 2005, and Mars Odyssey, launched in 2001. These spacecraft continue to support scientific research and rover communications.

MAVEN exceeded its original two-year mission timeline by operating successfully for more than a decade. The extended mission allowed scientists to gather substantially more data about the Martian atmosphere than initially planned, making the orbiter one of NASA's longest-serving Mars missions.

NASA has not disclosed what caused the spacecraft to stop responding or detailed any recovery attempts made before declaring the mission concluded. The space agency indicated that more information would be shared once the investigation progresses and the agency completes its assessment of what happened to MAVEN during its fateful pass behind the red planet.

cards.headline: House passes resolution to limit Trump war powers during Iran negotiations
cards.body:
The House of Representatives voted 215 to 208 to advance a war powers resolution that would force President Trump to seek congressional approval or withdraw U.S. forces from the ongoing conflict with Iran. The measure passed with support from all Democrats and four Republicans who broke ranks with their party.

The four Republican dissidents were Thomas Massie of Kentucky, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Warren Davidson of Ohio, and Tom Barrett of Michigan. The resolution now moves to the Senate for consideration.

Trump responded swiftly to the House action on Thursday, dismissing the vote as meaningless and criticizing the timing. He characterized the four Republicans who supported the measure as "bad Republicans" and questioned their patriotism, asking "who would do such an unpatriotic thing." The president stated that the vote came at a critical moment in his final negotiations with Iran and argued that the Republicans "know where the negotiations stand."

The vote represents the fourth congressional effort to constrain Trump's war powers regarding the Iran conflict. The timing is significant because the War Powers Resolution of 1973 requires presidents to seek congressional approval to continue military operations after 90 days of hostilities. The Iran war has now exceeded that threshold, though the White House has contested this requirement by citing a temporary ceasefire that took effect on April 8, despite multiple breaches by the United States, Israel, and Iran.

While the resolution is largely symbolic and faces an uncertain path in the Senate, it demonstrates rare fracturing within Republican ranks on military matters. The four Republican defections underscore growing congressional concern about the scope and duration of the Iran operation.

The House action comes as the Trump administration simultaneously pursues broader Middle East negotiations. The administration announced an agreement between Israel and Lebanon to implement a ceasefire, though the deal carries significant conditions. The ceasefire is contingent on complete cessation of fire from the Iran-aligned Hezbollah armed group and the evacuation of all its fighters from south of the Litani River in southern Lebanon.

However, the ceasefire agreement has proven fragile. Despite the announced deal, Israel carried out drone strikes in southern Lebanon on Thursday morning, striking what the military characterized as Hezbollah infrastructure near Tyre. The military acknowledged that a hospital was "affected incidentally" and accused Hezbollah of occupying the facility.

Reports indicate that three hospitals in southern Lebanon have been attacked by Israeli forces within a week, resulting in more than 150 wounded and nine deaths. Analysts and human rights experts have suggested the attacks on healthcare facilities aimed to degrade living conditions in southern Lebanon.

cards.headline: House votes to block further military strikes on Iran
cards.body:
The House of Representatives passed a measure seeking to halt additional military action against Iran, delivering a rebuke to President Trump. The vote included four Republicans who broke with the president, prompting his public criticism.

Trump responded to the vote by calling it "unpatriotic" and singling out the Republicans who voted against him. The lower chamber of Congress passed the measure in what observers described as a largely symbolic vote. The president has faced what multiple sources characterized as a legislative losing streak, with his influence over Congress appearing to weaken.

The four Republicans who opposed Trump on the Iran vote now face what reports described as his wrath. Trump publicly criticized these lawmakers, referring to them as "bad Republicans" for their decision to support ending the war in Iran. The vote represents a notable break within the Republican party on foreign policy.

The measure comes as Israel and Lebanon have reached an agreement that could help end the war in Iran, though implementation of the ceasefire has stalled. The U.N. peacekeeping mission for Lebanon reported that one peacekeeper was killed and others were wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon.

Senate Republicans are separately moving forward on a bill to fund immigration enforcement through the end of Trump's term. The Senate dropped Trump ballroom funding from the immigration bill and is set to begin debate on ICE funding. The chamber is preparing for what lawmakers called a vote-a-rama on the budget bill.

cards.headline: Senate to begin debate on immigration enforcement funding
cards.teaser: Senate Republicans are advancing a bill to fund ICE through the end of President Trump's term.
cards.body:
Senate Republicans are advancing legislation to fund immigration enforcement operations through the end of Trump's presidential term. The Senate is preparing to begin debate on the ICE funding measure.

Senate Republicans removed Trump ballroom funding from the immigration bill before moving it forward for consideration.

cards.headline: Israel and Hezbollah Exchange Strikes After Lebanon Cease-Fire
cards.teaser: Hezbollah's leader said the group rejected a U.S.-brokered deal that did not include the Iran-backed militia.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a cease-fire, with both countries rejecting "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage," according to the U.S. However, Hezbollah, the Iran-backed militia excluded from U.S.-brokered negotiations, rejected the deal and continued attacks despite the formal agreement taking effect.

Violence persisted even as the cease-fire began. A U.N. peacekeeper was killed and others wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon, according to UNIFIL, the U.N. peacekeeping mission there.

cards.headline: Hezbollah rejects terms of Israel-Lebanon ceasefire agreement
cards.teaser: The militia declined conditions requiring it to halt attacks and withdraw from southern Lebanon.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a ceasefire contingent on Hezbollah halting attacks and withdrawing from south of the Litani River. The agreement was outlined in a joint statement from the U.S., Israel, and Lebanon, which rejected "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage."

However, Hezbollah objected to the specific conditions of the agreement. While the group had previously signaled willingness to accept a full ceasefire, it did not accept the terms as negotiated between the Israeli and Lebanese governments.

cards.headline: Israel and Lebanon agree to ceasefire, but implementation stalls
cards.teaser: Israel and Lebanon reached a ceasefire agreement, though the implementation has not moved forward.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have reached a ceasefire agreement, contingent on Hezbollah halting its attacks. The U.S. has stated that both countries reject any attempt by state or non-state actors to control Lebanon's future.

However, the ceasefire has not yet been implemented. The U.N. peacekeeping mission in Lebanon, UNIFIL, reported that one peacekeeper was killed and several others wounded after coming under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon.

hero.headline: Gun Battles Erupt in Mogadishu as Election Dispute Escalates
hero.body:
Armed groups loyal to rival politicians clashed in Somalia's capital on Thursday, producing what residents described as the worst fighting in years. The violence erupted as tensions escalated over the president's decision to extend his term in office by one year, a move that has drawn opposition protests and accusations of undermining the democratic process.

The gun battles broke out across Mogadishu, with heavy gunfire reported in multiple neighborhoods. The fighting pits forces aligned with the sitting president against those backing opposition politicians who reject the term extension. The opposition has called for demonstrations against what it views as an illegal power grab, setting the stage for further unrest in the Horn of Africa nation.

The extension of the presidential term has plunged Somalia into a political crisis at a time when the country faces ongoing security challenges. The delay in elections has fractured the fragile political consensus that had held among Somali leaders. Residents have expressed fear that the violence could spiral into broader conflict, threatening the stability of a city that has endured decades of warfare.

Somalia has struggled to hold timely elections, with previous votes also facing delays due to disputes over the electoral process and security concerns. The country operates under a complex indirect voting system in which clan elders select members of parliament, who then choose the president. Direct popular elections remain a distant goal in a nation still grappling with the insurgency of the militant group al-Shabab.

The international community has expressed concern over the political standoff and the outbreak of violence. Foreign governments and international organizations have urged Somali leaders to resolve their differences through dialogue and to proceed with elections as quickly as possible. The fighting underscores the fragility of Somalia's political system and the risks that disputes among elites pose to ordinary citizens caught in the crossfire.

cards.headline: Israel and Hezbollah Exchange Strikes After Lebanon Cease-Fire
cards.teaser: Hezbollah's leader said the group rejected a U.S.-brokered deal that did not include the Iran-backed militia.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a cease-fire, with both countries rejecting "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage," according to the U.S. However, Hezbollah, the Iran-backed militia excluded from U.S.-brokered negotiations, rejected the deal and continued attacks despite the formal agreement taking effect.

cards.headline: Graphic Novelist Marjane Satrapi Dies at 56
cards.teaser: The author of Persepolis created a popular series following an Iranian girl through revolution and war.
cards.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian graphic novelist and filmmaker behind the acclaimed memoir Persepolis, has died at age 56. Her groundbreaking work helped reshape international perceptions of Iran through its intimate portrayal of life during the Islamic Revolution and Iran-Iraq War.

Satrapi's distinctive black-and-white illustrations and candid storytelling made Persepolis a landmark in graphic literature when it was published in the early 2000s. The series, which was adapted into an Oscar-nominated film, introduced readers worldwide to her experiences growing up in revolutionary Iran. According to her family, she died of sadness following the death of her husband, Swedish producer Mattias Ripa, last year.

cards.headline: Priest's Ebola Death Raises Alarm in Congolese Town
cards.teaser: The death has stirred fear and doubt among residents in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
cards.body:
A priest has died of Ebola in a town in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to reports. The death has created anxiety among residents in the affected community.

The case raises concerns about a potential outbreak in the region. Congo has faced multiple Ebola epidemics in recent years, with the highly lethal virus posing persistent public health challenges in eastern parts of the country.

cards.headline: Ukraine Accused of Attacks Killing Four in Occupied Crimea
cards.teaser: Russian-backed officials say at least 10 people were injured in the strikes.
cards.body:
Russian-backed officials in occupied Crimea accused Ukraine of carrying out attacks that killed four people. At least 10 others were injured in the incidents, according to the officials.

The accusation adds to the ongoing tensions over the peninsula, which Russia seized from Ukraine in 2014. Ukraine has not confirmed responsibility for the attacks. Such strikes in Crimea have become more frequent as the conflict continues.

cards.headline: Trump Endorses Dual Citizen in Colombian Presidential Runoff
cards.teaser: Abelardo De La Espriella holds citizenship in both Colombia and the United States.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Abelardo De La Espriella, a right-wing candidate in Colombia's presidential runoff election. De La Espriella is a dual citizen of Colombia and the United States, raising questions about his eligibility under Colombian law.

The endorsement marks a direct intervention by Trump in the election of a key South American nation. The candidate's dual citizenship status has become a point of controversy in the campaign, with legal experts debating whether it disqualifies him from holding the presidency.

cards.headline: Colombian Soccer Jersey Becomes Symbol in Charged Election
cards.teaser: A presidential candidate has been accused of co-opting the beloved yellow jersey worn by the national team.
cards.body:
The yellow jersey worn by Colombia's national soccer team has become a political flashpoint in the country's presidential campaign. A candidate endorsed by President Trump has been accused by some Colombians of appropriating the symbol for partisan purposes.

The jersey had long served as a unifying symbol for Colombians across political divides. Its use in the current campaign has divided opinion, with critics saying the candidate is exploiting national pride for electoral gain.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans oppose Trump intelligence chief pick
cards.teaser: Senate Republicans are rebelling against President Trump's choice of Bill Pulte for national intelligence director.
cards.body:
Republican backlash has intensified over Trump's selection of Bill Pulte for the national intelligence director role. Sources described the new intel chief as a partisan warrior who has the president's ear.

Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell issued a statement that suggested he considers Pulte unfit for the national intelligence director position. The pick has sparked what reports characterized as a Senate GOP rebellion against the president's nominee.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm confirmed in Texas calf
cards.teaser: The USDA confirmed a case of the New World screwworm, a flesh-eating parasite, in cattle in Texas.
cards.body:
A New World screwworm has been confirmed in a calf in south Texas, roughly 50 miles from the Mexico border, marking the first case in U.S. cattle in six decades, agriculture officials announced. The USDA and Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins confirmed the discovery of the flesh-eating parasite.

The reappearance of the New World screwworm represents a significant concern for the U.S. livestock industry. The parasite had been eradicated from the country and its return signals a potential threat to cattle herds across the nation.

cards.headline: Gun control group sues ATF over crime gun seller records
cards.teaser: Brady is suing federal agencies for refusing to release information about the largest sellers of crime guns in the United States.
cards.body:
Brady, a nonprofit gun control advocacy group, is suing the ATF and the Department of Justice for refusing to release documents about the largest sellers of crime guns in the United States. The lawsuit aims to compel the federal agencies to disclose these records, which Brady believes should be accessible to the public.

The case centers on transparency regarding firearms used in crimes and who supplies them into the criminal market.

cards.teaser: Israel and Lebanon reached a ceasefire agreement, though the implementation has not moved forward.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have reached a ceasefire agreement, contingent on Hezbollah halting its attacks. The U.S. has stated that both countries reject any attempt by state or non-state actors to control Lebanon's future.

Senate Republicans are advancing legislation to fund immigration enforcement operations through the end of Trump's presidential term. The Senate is preparing to begin debate on the ICE funding measure.

cards.headline: Graphic novelist Marjane Satrapi dies at 56
cards.teaser: The French-Iranian author and illustrator known for Persepolis has died.
cards.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian graphic novelist and filmmaker, died at age 56. She was best known for creating Persepolis, an acclaimed autobiographical graphic novel that helped reshape international perceptions of Iran. The work was adapted into a film that received an Oscar nomination.

According to her family, Satrapi died of sadness following the death of her husband, Swedish producer Mattias Ripa, the previous year. Her landmark comic book memoir drew on her experiences and became internationally recognized for its artistic and cultural significance.

hero.headline: Stock market splits as Broadcom earnings send chip stocks down, Dow up 700 points
hero.body:
The stock market divided sharply as semiconductor stocks fell while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 700 points. The S&P 500 declined as Broadcom led a selloff in chip stocks during trading. The contrasting moves highlighted a split between technology and other sectors.

Broadcom led losses among chipmakers in premarket trading, with Micron and Marvell also falling. The decline followed Broadcom's earnings report, which disappointed investors. The semiconductor sector's weakness pulled the Nasdaq down while the Dow gained ground.

The divergence between the Dow and Nasdaq represented a shift in market leadership. While technology stocks struggled, other sectors drove the Dow's advance. The S&P 500, which includes both technology and traditional industrial companies, fell as the chip selloff outweighed gains elsewhere.

Oil prices dropped from recent highs as stocks showed mixed performance. Reuters reported that stocks struggled after Broadcom's decline, with energy markets also pulling back. The mixed trading session came after the S&P 500 had recently reached record levels.

The market movement reflected investor reassessment of technology valuations following Broadcom's results. Bloomberg and Yahoo Finance both reported the premarket losses among major semiconductor companies. The 700-point Dow gain stood in contrast to the technology sector's weakness, showing how different parts of the market can move in opposite directions based on sector-specific news.

cards.headline: SpaceX targets $135 share price for IPO at $1.77 trillion valuation
cards.teaser: SpaceX set its initial public offering price at $135 per share, aiming for what would become the largest stock market debut in history.
cards.body:
SpaceX established a target price of $135 per share for its initial public offering, according to the company's prospectus. The pricing would value the company at $1.77 trillion, making it the biggest market debut ever. CBS News reported the IPO could make Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire.

The company released a 17-minute video pitch to promote the offering, Bloomberg reported. Fortune noted that a single sentence in the amended IPO filing could signal a major merger ahead. The New York Times described the filing as reflecting confidence in the planned market debut, though some observers expressed concerns about the valuation.

cards.headline: Trump administration pushes to expand AI use in American medicine
cards.teaser: A Trump-backed initiative aims to bring artificial intelligence doctors into medical practice across the United States.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is advancing an effort to introduce AI doctors into American healthcare. The Washington Post reported the push represents a significant shift in how medical care could be delivered. Healthcare Dive noted that AI adoption is surging, though healthcare providers have expressed concerns about deskilling.

Doctors have issued warnings about using AI in healthcare, with ABC4 Utah reporting that medical professionals called it a very bad thing. MIT Technology Review discussed rehumanizing global healthcare with what it termed agentic AI. Harvard Business Review examined how agentic AI could drive measurable business value in healthcare enterprises.

cards.headline: Quantinuum prices IPO at $60 per share, set to begin trading
cards.teaser: Quantinuum, a quantum computing company formerly part of Honeywell, priced its initial public offering at $60 per share ahead of its Nasdaq debut.
cards.body:
Quantinuum priced its initial public offering at $60 per share ahead of its Thursday market debut. The quantum computing company raised $1.68 billion through the offering, which was oversubscribed 20 times, reflecting strong investor demand for the sector.

The IPO comes as quantum computing continues gaining traction in the technology industry. The listing positions Quantinuum among a growing number of quantum companies attracting capital from investors betting on the technology's future applications.

cards.headline: Stock rally created 2 million new millionaires worldwide last year
cards.teaser: Soaring stock prices generated 2 million new millionaires around the world over the past year, driven largely by the artificial intelligence boom.
cards.body:
Rising stock markets minted 2 million new millionaires globally over the past year, driven largely by enthusiasm around artificial intelligence investments. The AI boom has fueled wealth creation at the fastest pace in four years, particularly among US investors.

The surge in wealth reflects concentrated gains in technology and AI-related stocks. Meanwhile, the super wealthy are pulling further ahead of the broader rich, widening the gap between the most affluent and those newly entering millionaire status.

cards.headline: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square exits Universal Music stake with $600 million gain
cards.teaser: Pershing Square is set to make $600 million after selling its stake in Universal Music Group following a rejected takeover bid.
cards.body:
Bill Ackman's Pershing Square will realize a $600 million gain from selling its stake in Universal Music Group, following the company's rejection of his takeover proposal valued at $64 billion. Universal Music shares dropped 7 percent as Pershing Square offloaded its position after the failed acquisition attempts.

The exit marks the end of Ackman's effort to acquire the music giant, which repeatedly turned down his bid to take the company private.

cards.headline: Pace Gallery cuts 50 artists and 50 staff amid art market downturn
cards.teaser: The established art gallery is reducing its roster of artists and employees in response to difficult market conditions.
cards.body:
Pace Gallery announced it is cutting 50 artists from its roster and eliminating 50 staff positions. The reductions come as the art market faces challenges, forcing even established players to contract operations.

The gallery's decision reflects broader difficulties in the art market. The cuts affect both the creative talent the gallery represents and its workforce, signaling the depth of the market pressures facing the industry.

cards.headline: Geomagnetic storm forecast to bring northern lights to 23 states
cards.teaser: A strong geomagnetic storm could make the aurora borealis visible across parts of the northern United States.
cards.body:
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration upgraded its geomagnetic storm watch to G3 level, indicating strong solar activity that could bring northern lights displays to 23 states. The forecast covers viewing opportunities for Vermont, New York, New Hampshire, and other northern tier states.

The geomagnetic storm results from solar activity that sends charged particles toward Earth. When these particles interact with the planet's magnetic field and atmosphere, they create the colorful light displays known as auroras. The G3 watch classification suggests the storm could produce visible auroras at lower latitudes than typical displays.

cards.headline: Meteorite found in Sahara may provide evidence of lost solar system planet
cards.teaser: A rare meteorite discovered in the Sahara desert could be the first evidence of an ancient rocky world that once existed in our solar system.
cards.body:
Scientists analyzing a meteorite found in the Sahara desert believe it may represent fragments from a previously unknown planetary body that existed in the early solar system. The rare specimen suggests the solar system might be missing a rocky planet that formed billions of years ago but no longer exists.

The meteorite's composition differs from known classifications of space rocks, leading researchers to conclude it originated from a distinct parent body. The discovery hints at a giant early planet that may have been destroyed in a collision or other catastrophic event during the solar system's formation period. The fragment provides physical evidence that our solar system's architecture was more complex in its youth than the current arrangement of eight planets suggests.

cards.headline: Oura releases Ring 5 as smallest smart ring on market
cards.teaser: The fitness tracking company launched a redesigned smart ring that is 40 percent smaller than the previous model.
cards.body:
Oura unveiled the Ring 5, positioning it as the world's smallest smart ring on the market. The new device is 40 percent smaller than its predecessor while maintaining a thinner, lighter design. The Ring 5 starts at $399.

The reduced size reflects Oura's commitment to the smart ring form factor for fitness tracking. The company has addressed user demands for improved comfort and aesthetics without compromising the core health and sleep monitoring features that define the product line.

cards.headline: Google releases technical specifications for third-party Fitbit Air accessories
cards.teaser: The company published CAD drawings and design guidelines allowing anyone to create custom bands and accessories for its fitness tracker.
cards.body:
Google released CAD drawings and technical specifications for the Fitbit Air, enabling independent manufacturers and individuals to design their own bands and accessories for the device. The blueprints include detailed measurements and design guidelines for creating compatible products, including support for bicep band attachments.

The move opens the Fitbit Air to a broader accessory ecosystem beyond Google's official offerings. Users can now 3D print their own accessories or purchase custom designs from third-party creators who follow the published specifications. The company provided the technical documentation publicly, allowing makers and manufacturers to develop products that properly fit the wearable device.

cards.headline: Nintendo confirms Switch 2 model with replaceable battery for European market
cards.teaser: The gaming company will sell a version of its upcoming console with user-replaceable batteries to comply with European Union regulations.
cards.body:
Nintendo is planning to launch versions of Switch 2 in the EU with user-replaceable batteries to comply with new European regulations taking effect February 18, 2027. The company confirmed on its website that it is "implementing measures to comply with these requirements."

The regulation requires electronic devices sold in the EU to have batteries that users can easily replace. Nintendo's design registration with EU authorities shows the company will produce a Switch 2 model meeting this standard for the European market.

cards.headline: Waymo repurposes used robotaxi batteries for electrical grid storage
cards.teaser: The autonomous vehicle company will supply second-life batteries from its fleet to energy storage projects in California and Texas.
cards.body:
Waymo announced a program to convert used batteries from its robotaxi fleet into backup storage systems for electrical power grids. The batteries will support energy storage projects in California and Texas, extending their useful life after they no longer meet the performance requirements for autonomous vehicles.

The initiative addresses both electronic waste reduction and grid stability needs. Batteries that decline below the threshold needed for vehicle operation still retain significant storage capacity suitable for stationary applications. The second-life program allows the batteries to serve an additional function before eventual recycling, while helping utilities manage peak demand and integrate renewable energy sources.

hero.headline: Knicks defeat Spurs in Game 1 of NBA Finals behind Brunson's performance
hero.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 105-95 in Game 1 of the NBA Finals on Wednesday night in San Antonio, maintaining an 11-game winning streak that has dominated the postseason. Jalen Brunson led the Knicks to victory with 30 points, including 13 in the fourth quarter as New York pulled away from their opponents.

The game proved competitive throughout, with the Spurs holding a 14-point lead in the third quarter before the Knicks mounted their comeback. The fourth quarter became decisive, as New York went on an 11-0 run to secure the win. The Knicks also benefited from strong performances by OG Anunoby, who scored 12 of his 17 points in the final quarter, and maintained a crucial advantage by committing zero turnovers in the fourth quarter.

"Just sticking together, it wasn't really our night and wasn't really my night most of the night but we kept finding a way, kept chipping away," Brunson said after the game. "Just knowing we have each other's back, there's a lot of things we could have done better, but I think our togetherness was really the biggest difference."

The Spurs struggled down the stretch, committing five turnovers in the fourth quarter while shooting just 28.6 percent. Victor Wembanyama, the Spurs' young superstar and the league's most exciting player, led San Antonio with 26 points, 12 rebounds and three blocks but shot just 6-for-21 from the field. Wembanyama briefly left the court with an injury scare in the third quarter before returning.

"I was bad tonight, it's not more complicated than that," Wembanyama said afterward. He dismissed suggestions that the occasion affected the Spurs' performance, denying that nerves played a role in their loss.

Brunson dealt with injury concerns of his own when he collided with San Antonio's Harrison Barnes at the end of the first quarter, leaving the game with a knee injury. He returned in the second quarter and appeared to hurt his ankle on a layup attempt but remained in the game.

The victory moves the Knicks within three wins of their first NBA championship since 1973, ending a 53-year title drought. The series comes after the Spurs knocked out the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder in the previous round.

Game 2 is scheduled for Friday night in San Antonio before the best-of-seven series moves to Madison Square Garden on Monday. The Knicks' strong fourth-quarter performance and their ability to overcome significant deficits positions them well as they pursue their first championship in over five decades.

cards.headline: Former Ireland and Lions rugby player Fergus Slattery dies at 77
cards.teaser: Fergus Slattery, who played back row for Ireland and the British and Irish Lions, has died at age 77.
cards.body:
Blackrock College has announced the death of Fergus Slattery, the former Ireland and British and Irish Lions back row, who was 77 years old.

Slattery enjoyed a distinguished rugby career representing both his country and the prestigious Lions touring side during his playing days.

cards.headline: Patriots acquire wide receiver A.J. Brown from Eagles in trade
cards.teaser: The New England Patriots obtained wide receiver A.J. Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in a trade that drew mixed reactions.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles traded wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots in a deal that has generated varied responses around both organizations. Eagles left tackle Jordan Mailata expressed relief following the transaction, stating he was glad the situation had concluded.

The trade represents a significant roster move for both franchises. The Patriots are positioning themselves to compete for a championship with the addition of Brown, a proven receiver. Eagles players and coaches offered mixed reactions during organized team activities following the departure of the prominent offensive weapon.

cards.headline: Brighton reject Tottenham's opening bid for defender Jan Paul van Hecke
cards.teaser: Brighton turned down a 70 million pound offer from Tottenham for Netherlands defender Jan Paul van Hecke and expect a second bid.
cards.body:
Brighton have rejected Tottenham's opening bid of £70 million for defender Jan Paul van Hecke. The Premier League club expects Spurs to submit an improved offer for the Netherlands international.

The rejection suggests Brighton value the player significantly higher than Tottenham's initial proposal and are prepared to negotiate further with the north London club.

cards.headline: Manchester City chairman says Guardiola previously considered leaving multiple times
cards.teaser: Pep Guardiola had threatened to quit as Manchester City manager on numerous occasions before this season, according to chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.
cards.body:
Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak revealed that Pep Guardiola threatened to quit "100 times" during his tenure at the club. Al Mubarak compared the repeated threats to The Boy Who Cried Wolf, suggesting many were not serious. The chairman described himself as Guardiola's "psychiatrist" and was instrumental in convincing him to stay on multiple occasions.

Guardiola left Manchester City last month after 10 years, during which he won 17 major honours. He initially signed a three-year contract but agreed to four extensions in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024, each time showing hesitation about his future at the club.

cards.headline: Formula 1 driver Valtteri Bottas denies reports about Cadillac exit
cards.teaser: Valtteri Bottas dismissed rumors suggesting he might leave the Cadillac Formula 1 team, calling the reports fabricated.
cards.body:
Valtteri Bottas rejected speculation about his future with the Cadillac Formula 1 team, using strong language to describe the rumors as false and created for headlines and clicks. The Finnish driver addressed the reports directly, denying any plans to depart the organization.

Bottas characterized the exit rumors as completely fabricated stories with no basis in fact. The driver made his position clear while in Monaco, pushing back against multiple media outlets that had raised questions about his status with Cadillac for the remainder of the season.

cards.headline: Mark McCall hopes for final trophy before departing Saracens
cards.teaser: Saracens director of rugby Mark McCall is aiming to win one more trophy before stepping down from his role.
cards.body:
Mark McCall is stepping down as Saracens' director of rugby and wants to win one last trophy before he leaves. He has been a significant figure at the club, guiding them through challenging times.

McCall has identified the unity Saracens displayed during their salary cap scandal as his proudest achievement in his time with the organization. He now hopes to end his tenure on a high note by securing silverware in the current season.

hero.headline: Marjane Satrapi, Oscar-Nominated Persepolis Creator, Dies at 56
hero.body:
Marjane Satrapi, the French-Iranian artist and graphic novelist best known for her groundbreaking memoir Persepolis, has died at age 56. Her family stated that she "died of sadness" following the death of her husband, Swedish producer Mattias Ripa, who passed away on April 8 of the previous year.

Born in 1969 in Rasht, Iran, Satrapi was raised in Tehran by her father, an engineer, and her mother, a dress designer. As a teenager, her parents sent her to Europe to continue her education and escape the restrictions of Iran's Islamic Republic. She eventually settled in France in 1994 and became a French citizen in 2006.

Satrapi gained international acclaim with Persepolis, a graphic novel memoir published in 2000. The work tells the story of a rebellious young girl navigating Iran's upheaval following the 1979 revolution and the establishment of the Islamic Republic, before being sent alone to Europe at age 14. The memoir became an international publishing phenomenon, selling millions of copies and establishing Satrapi as one of the most widely read Iranian authors globally.

In a 2020 interview, Satrapi reflected on her unlikely success, saying she initially had little expectation the work would reach publication. "With Persepolis, I didn't even think I'd find a publisher. I thought I'd make 50 photocopies for my friends to read," she told El País.

The 2007 animated film adaptation, which Satrapi co-directed with Vincent Paronnaud, became an international success. It earned Satrapi a place in Oscar history as the first woman nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

Satrapi later directed five feature films, including the 2019 biopic Radioactive, starring Rosamund Pike as Marie Curie. In recent years, she returned to comics, coordinating Woman, Life, Freedom in 2024, a collaborative graphic work bringing together 17 Iranian and international artists to examine the protest movement following the death of Mahsa Amini in 2022.

Discussing her choice of medium, Satrapi once explained that drawing represented humanity's first language, preceding writing and speech. Throughout her career, she emphasized that her work aimed to reassure young Iranians they were heard and supported by the outside world.

President Emmanuel Macron paid tribute to Satrapi, describing her as "a great artist who turned her Iranian childhood into a universal tale." Her work challenged Western assumptions about Iranian society and culture, earning widespread recognition for its ability to convey complex historical and personal experiences through illustration and narrative.

cards.headline: Writers Guild Criticizes CBS News Layoffs and Scott Pelley Firing
cards.teaser: The union representing writers condemned Paramount-owned CBS News for recent job cuts and the termination of longtime correspondent Scott Pelley.
cards.body:
Tom Fontana, president of the Writers Guild of America East, condemned CBS News for recent layoffs, the firing of 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley, and the shutdown of CBS News Radio, characterizing the actions as showing contempt for journalism.

Pelley accused CBS News executives of instructing him to inject falsehoods and bias into his reporting. He stated that 60 Minutes has remained America's top-rated program because audiences value its integrity and quality, suggesting the network's new management has compromised those principles.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Criticized White House Use of Her Song for ICE Promotion
cards.teaser: The pop star told Dazed magazine she was enraged when the Trump administration used her music to promote immigration enforcement activities.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo discovered while scrolling through her phone last fall that the Trump administration's Department of Homeland Security had used her song "All-American Bitch" in materials promoting Immigration and Customs Enforcement deportations. She told Dazed magazine that the use of her music deeply disturbed her.

Rodrigo expressed strong anger over the association between her work and the administration's immigration enforcement actions, characterizing what the government is doing as "awful, barbaric and cruel." She is currently preparing to release her third studio album.

cards.headline: Snap Acquires Augmented Reality Company Illumix
cards.teaser: The parent company of Snapchat purchased the spatial AR firm to enhance its augmented reality capabilities and mapping technology.
cards.body:
Snap acquired Illumix, a company specializing in spatial augmented reality technology. The deal was driven by Illumix's work in developing mapping technology and building platforms for real-world augmented reality experiences.

Snap plans to integrate Illumix's technology and platform into its existing operations as it expands its AR offerings. The acquisition reflects Snap's continued investment in augmented reality capabilities for its Snapchat platform and other products.

cards.headline: Helen Mirren and Russell Crowe to Attend Taormina Film Festival
cards.teaser: The Italian festival announced its lineup for the 72nd edition, featuring appearances by major actors and a mix of commercial and art house films.
cards.body:
Helen Mirren, Russell Crowe, Scott Eastwood, and Gore Verbinski are scheduled to attend the Taormina Film Festival in Italy. The festival unveiled its lineup for the 72nd edition, which combines mainstream films with more specialized fare.

Crowe's attendance had been announced previously. The festival, considered a significant event in the Italian cinema calendar, will showcase various international productions during its run.

cards.headline: Barack Obama Appears on Malcolm Gladwell Reconstruction Podcast
cards.teaser: The former president joined the author for an eight-part series examining the post-Civil War era, produced by Higher Ground and the History Channel.
cards.body:
Barack Obama is featured in Reconstruction: The Unfinished Promise, a new podcast hosted by Malcolm Gladwell. The eight-part series is a collaboration between the History Channel, Barack and Michelle Obama's Higher Ground production company, Gladwell's Pushkin Industries, and Audible.

The podcast examines the Reconstruction era following the Civil War. The series began airing Thursday and explores themes related to that period in American history.

cards.headline: Scary Movie Sequel Returns to Ghostface Parody Format
cards.teaser: The sixth installment of the franchise, written by multiple members of the Wayans family, focuses heavily on the Scream film series.
cards.body:
The latest Scary Movie film, scripted by Marlon Wayans, Shawn Wayans, Keenen Ivory Wayans, Craig Wayans, and Rick Alvarez, centers its comedy on the Ghostface character from the Scream franchise. The film includes jokes about the number of Wayans family members involved in the production.

Reviewers noted that the movie maintains a tone of comic aggression through repeated appearances by the Ghostface killer. The film's focus on parodying the Scream series dominates its comedy approach throughout.

hero.headline: House passes resolution to limit Trump war powers during Iran negotiations
hero.body:
The House of Representatives voted 215 to 208 to advance a war powers resolution that would force President Trump to seek congressional approval or withdraw U.S. forces from the ongoing conflict with Iran. The measure passed with support from all Democrats and four Republicans who broke ranks with their party.

The four Republican dissidents were Thomas Massie of Kentucky, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Warren Davidson of Ohio, and Tom Barrett of Michigan. The resolution now moves to the Senate for consideration.

Trump responded swiftly to the House action on Thursday, dismissing the vote as meaningless and criticizing the timing. He characterized the four Republicans who supported the measure as "bad Republicans" and questioned their patriotism, asking "who would do such an unpatriotic thing." The president stated that the vote came at a critical moment in his final negotiations with Iran and argued that the Republicans "know where the negotiations stand."

The vote represents the fourth congressional effort to constrain Trump's war powers regarding the Iran conflict. The timing is significant because the War Powers Resolution of 1973 requires presidents to seek congressional approval to continue military operations after 90 days of hostilities. The Iran war has now exceeded that threshold, though the White House has contested this requirement by citing a temporary ceasefire that took effect on April 8, despite multiple breaches by the United States, Israel, and Iran.

While the resolution is largely symbolic and faces an uncertain path in the Senate, it demonstrates rare fracturing within Republican ranks on military matters. The four Republican defections underscore growing congressional concern about the scope and duration of the Iran operation.

The House action comes as the Trump administration simultaneously pursues broader Middle East negotiations. The administration announced an agreement between Israel and Lebanon to implement a ceasefire, though the deal carries significant conditions. The ceasefire is contingent on complete cessation of fire from the Iran-aligned Hezbollah armed group and the evacuation of all its fighters from south of the Litani River in southern Lebanon.

However, the ceasefire agreement has proven fragile. Despite the announced deal, Israel carried out drone strikes in southern Lebanon on Thursday morning, striking what the military characterized as Hezbollah infrastructure near Tyre. The military acknowledged that a hospital was "affected incidentally" and accused Hezbollah of occupying the facility.

Reports indicate that three hospitals in southern Lebanon have been attacked by Israeli forces within a week, resulting in more than 150 wounded and nine deaths. Analysts and human rights experts have suggested the attacks on healthcare facilities aimed to degrade living conditions in southern Lebanon.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden Interior Secretary secured the Democratic nomination in New Mexico's gubernatorial race.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary under President Biden, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. She will advance to the general election as her party's nominee.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history. She previously served as a U.S. Representative for New Mexico before joining the Biden administration.

---

Note: The additional source material provided does not contain relevant information about Deb Haaland's gubernatorial campaign. The sources discuss an unrelated missing person case in New Mexico and Senate budget disputes. Therefore, I have returned the original card text unchanged, as instructed.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton lead California governor primary
cards.teaser: Early results show the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom taking shape.
cards.body:
Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton are leading California's primary election for governor. Polls show Hilton with a narrow lead, followed by Becerra, with billionaire Democrat Tom Steyer trailing behind.

Under California's top-two primary system, the highest vote-getters will advance to the general election regardless of party. State election officials continue counting uncounted ballots, a process that could take days or weeks. The winner will replace term-limited Governor Gavin Newsom.

cards.headline: Lauren Boebert criticizes Tom Kean Jr. for absence from Capitol Hill
cards.teaser: The Colorado Republican questioned her New Jersey colleague's extended time away from Washington and the campaign trail.
cards.body:
Representative Lauren Boebert of Colorado criticized fellow Republican Representative Tom Kean Jr. of New Jersey for his extended absence from Capitol Hill and the campaign trail. "Where is he? No, seriously. It's embarrassing," Boebert told reporters.

Boebert's comments highlight tensions within the GOP over candidate visibility and engagement on the campaign trail.

cards.headline: USDA Secretary testifies on budget cuts before House committee
cards.teaser: Brooke Rollins faced questions about a proposed $4.9 billion reduction in department funding.
cards.body:
Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins testified before a House panel Thursday on the USDA's domestic priorities and the Trump administration's fiscal 2027 budget request. The administration is seeking $20.8 billion in discretionary budget authority for the department, representing a $4.9 billion decrease from the 2026 budget.

Rollins addressed how the department plans to maintain operations and fulfill its responsibilities amid the proposed funding reduction.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary testifies on department priorities amid Iran war
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent appeared before the House Ways and Means Committee for a second day of congressional testimony.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent testified before the House Ways and Means Committee on Thursday regarding President Trump's fiscal 2027 budget request and Treasury Department priorities. The hearing comes as the administration navigates economic policy during an ongoing military conflict in Iran.

The Treasury chief's House appearance followed earlier Senate testimony. His testimony addressed affordability and inflation concerns, key issues as the department manages economic challenges amid the Middle East crisis.

cards.headline: Screwworm parasite detected in Texas cattle for first time in decades
cards.teaser: The USDA confirmed a case of the flesh-eating fly in a calf southwest of San Antonio.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed the detection of a New World screwworm in a calf in south Texas, roughly 50 miles from the Mexico border. This marks the first confirmed case of the flesh-eating parasite in the state in six decades.

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins announced the discovery on Wednesday. The parasite poses a significant threat to the U.S. cattle industry, as the New World screwworm had been largely eradicated from the country for decades.
